I farm a small wheat-maize rotation on 8.7 mu, and I have done this for many years, so I will keep the land in the same double-cropping system. I have well irrigation, so I will use it to protect yield at the key stages instead of gambling on rainfall. Because my household labor is limited and I am 66, I will keep management practical and familiar rather than complicated. For wheat, I will use improved seed, give moderate fertilizer with more nitrogen than phosphorus and potassium, irrigate a few important times, and use rotary tillage because it is easier for me to manage than deep ploughing every season. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because I want stronger yield, keep fertilizer balanced but still nitrogen-focused, irrigate during the main water-demand periods, and continue rotary tillage after wheat. I will not overdo pesticide sprays; I will spray when needed to hold weeds, insects, and disease in check while keeping costs and labor manageable. My goal is stable yield from the full 8.7 mu, not risky high-input farming.
